folder_layout: raw_pattern/<CLASS_NAME>/*.jpg  (one folder per class, mirroring PatternType)
why_separate_from_fabric_family: Appearance is not provenance: 'striped' does not prove the cloth is Kente, and 'floral' does not automatically mean Ankara.
The acquired dataset labels what a photo LOOKS like, which is exactly this task — so this model trains first.
Keeping the two classifiers separate lets the app show them, fail, and say 'uncertain' independently.

collection_guidance.per_class_target: 300+ photos/class before training; 1000+ before claiming accuracy numbers
collection_guidance.label_the_dominant_visible_pattern: one class per photo; when two co-occur (stripes + dots), label the dominant one and log the mix in the filename
collection_guidance.plaid_vs_checked: CHECKED = simple alternating squares; PLAID = multi-colour crossed banding (kente-style/tartan-like). When unsure, prefer CHECKED.
collection_guidance.solid_is_a_class: plain cloths belong in SOLID — it is the honest 'no visible pattern' answer, not a reject pile
collection_guidance.crop_to_cloth: crop to the cloth/dress region; exclude hands, faces and backgrounds where possible (garment segmentation comes later)
collection_guidance.avoid: screens, prints of photos, watermarked stock, near-duplicate burst frames

uncertainty_contract.app_thresholds: TrainedModelRunner: top < 0.40 OR (top - second < 0.10 while top < 0.60) => reported as uncertain, never forced
uncertainty_contract.labels_file: pattern_labels.txt — one class name per line, in model output order, matching classes above
